profile.address: 14950, Kingsport Road, Fort Worth, Tarrant County, Texas, 76155
profile.reading: This record is named Cyxtera Dallas-Fort Worth Data Center in this registry, mapped to Tarrant County, Texas. No corporate website could be reached for this operator this session, and no independent secondary source describing this specific facility was found, so address, capacity, and square footage remain not published in this record. Cyxtera Technologies, headquartered in Coral Gables, Florida, entered into an Asset Purchase Agreement with Brookfield Infrastructure, disclosed via an SEC Form 8-K titled "Cyxtera x Brookfield APA Press Release" and filed November 2, 2023, per SEC EDGAR's full-text search index; this registry has not independently confirmed the full scope of that transaction (whether it covered Cyxtera's entire US colocation portfolio or a subset) beyond the filing's existence. Separately, Cologix, a different operator tracked elsewhere in this registry, acquired two specific Cyxtera facilities, VAN5 in Vancouver and MTL12 in Montreal, in 2023, per Cologix's own materials; those two Canadian facilities are unrelated to this Texas facility and to the Brookfield transaction. Cyxtera's own public website resolves but displays content that reads as dated (referencing a 2017 executive appointment) with no current facility locations list, and its data-centers subpage returns a certificate error, a combination consistent with a company mid-transition following the Brookfield transaction rather than one actively maintaining public marketing infrastructure. No square footage, MW capacity, or current operational status specific to this Dallas-Fort Worth facility was located in sourcing reachable this session. Fresh research this session, using web search tools unavailable in the prior exhausted pass, places this reverse geocoded Kingsport Road point near Cyxteras well documented DFW1 campus at 14901 FAA Blvd in Fort Worth, a single story purpose built facility rated at 51.9 megawatts about six miles from Dallas Fort Worth International Airport, though this entry cannot confirm this exact OSM footprint corresponds to that specific building rather than a nearby structure on the same campus, and does not assign the campus capacity figure to this row specifically. Cyxtera itself filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in June 2023; Brookfield Infrastructure Partners agreed to acquire seven of Cyxteras US data centers for 775 million dollars in a deal that closed in early 2024, merging retained Cyxtera facilities with Brookfields Evoque colocation platform into a combined operator later rebranded Centersquare with over 330 megawatts of combined North American capacity.

Page gives "133,298 sq. ft." raised floor, "51.9MW" Utility power, "16.4MW" UPS capacity, and "24MW" generator for Fort Worth DFW1 -- Utility/UPS figures explicitly separate labels, neither confirmed as "IT/critical load," so it_capacity_mw left empty; standby generator figure is unambiguous and written.

reading.body:
This campus publishes 51.9 megawatts of utility power and 16.4 megawatts of UPS capacity across 133,298 square feet of raised floor in Fort Worth, six miles from Dallas-Fort Worth International Airport. The published figures distinguish utility and UPS separately, so IT load capacity remains unconfirmed; assuming 40 kilowatts per rack, a common AI training density, the utility figure suggests roughly 1,300 racks at full density. The site holds NVIDIA DGX-Ready certification, qualifying it to host AI accelerator workloads, and carries SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, and NIST 800-53 PE High certifications for regulated tenants.

The facility operates under Centersquare, formed in 2024 when Brookfield Infrastructure merged its Evoque colocation platform with seven Cyxtera data centers acquired from bankruptcy for $775 million. Centersquare now operates over 330 megawatts across North America. This campus ranks 19th among the 18 facilities in Texas with published capacity, sitting outside the state's published capacity share despite its size, because most mapped facilities in the state publish no megawatt figure.

The 24-megawatt standby generator provides backup for grid outages, a standard feature for colocation but insufficient alone to sustain full-load operations. Whether this campus hosts AI training, inference, or general enterprise compute depends on tenant selection, which is not published. Texas holds 468 megawatts of published data center capacity across 133 mapped facilities; this site's utility power would represent 11 percent of the state's published total if it were on that list.
